 schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office. Meetings

 Administration Office at (818) 548-2107 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Glendale Water and Power Administration Office,
 141 N. Glendale Ave., Suite 450, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify

 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

MINUTES
  GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  CITY HALL - COUNCIL CHAMBER
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206

  Monday, October 05, 2020, 4:00 PM

1. ROLL CALL
  The meeting was called to order at 4:04 p.m.

  Present: President Pro Tem Lall, Commissioners Avanessian, Jazmadarian and Flanigan

  Absent: President Kedikian

2. GWP COMMISSION/ STAFF COMMENTS
  None.

3. REPORTS – INFORMATION
  a. Summer Heat Impacts
  Mr. Dan Scorza, Chief Assistant General Manager – Electric, described the challenges in
  providing electric service during two recent heat waves, occurring on August 18, 2020,
  when the temperature reached 108 degrees, and over Labor Day weekend, when the
  temperature reached 115 degrees. Mr. Scorza described several factors that affected
  GWP’s ability to serve load during the heat events, including generation, transmission,
  distribution system constraints. Mr. Scorza noted that GWP crews worked around the
  clock, and GWP customers were instrumental in conserving energy. Mr. Scorza and Mr.
  Mark Young, Deputy General Manager, responded to questions from the Commissioners.

  In response to questions from Commissioner Lall, Mr. Young clarified that a “stage 3
  CAISO alert” is the worst stage and means blackouts are imminent; and clarified that a
  Magnolia outage over Labor Day weekend was a 24-hour outage. In response to
  questions from Commissioner Avanessian, Mr. Scorza explained GWP’s practices for
  managing the load on transformers and its fire mitigation plan. In response to the
  questions from Commissioner Flannigan, Mr. Young explained that the lower peak load
  during the higher temperature event over Labor Day was a result of the fact that it was a
  weekend. Mr. Scorza explained that, while converting the system from 4kV to 12kV does
  not help during extreme heat events, the 12kV conversion is instrumental in reducing the
  system's amount of current flowing, making the system more efficient. The
  Commissioners congratulated GWP on keeping the system running and thanked
  customers for their role in conserving energy during the heat waves.

  1
 b. Water Resource Update
  Mr. Mike De Ghetto, Chief Assistant General Manager - Water, presented an update on
  GWP’s water resources and water supply outlook. Mr. De Ghetto covered GWP’s
  customer profile, which is mostly residential, and sources of water supply, including local
  groundwater from the San Fernando and Verdugo basins, recycled water, and water from
  the Metropolitan Water District (MWD). Mr. De Ghetto noted that 2020 was the hottest
  and driest summer for the Colorado Basin states (one of MWD’s water supply sources),
  but regional investments have allowed MWD to maintain storage to manage water supply.
  Mr. De Ghetto discussed future water projects at the local and regional level. He
  described the impact of conservation on water demand and presented historical and
  current annual trends in monthly potable water production. Mr. De Ghetto presented
  graphics showing usage patterns by type of customer and the correlation between single-
  family customer water consumption to weather and precipitation. Mr. De Ghetto noted that
  GWP’s water system has the highest complexity rating from the State of California for
  both distribution and treatment, based upon the City’s size and water treatment trains.

  Mr. Ghetto described GWP’s highly qualified water staff as the water department’s
  greatest resource. Mr. De Ghetto responded to questions from the Commissioners. In
  response to a question from Commissioner Avanessian, Mr. De Ghetto explained that the
  County actively manages rainwater capture at its spreading grounds. In response to a
  question from Commissioner Flanigan, Mr. De Ghetto provided some background on the
  20-year San Fernando Basin water rights litigation and the resulting judgment that
  provides Glendale with a 20% return flow credit. In response to a question from
  Commissioner Jazmadarian, Mr. De Ghetto provided information regarding the amount of
  recycled water available for GWP’s use and the factors that affect this, including the 211
  petitions, upgrades to the recycled water treatment plant, wastewater flows, and
  regulatory changes, among others; GWP’s goal is to use 100% of its recycled water. In
  response to Commissioner Jazmadarian’s question, Mr. De Ghetto provided background
  on GWP’s efforts to promote and retain qualified staff.

c. Strategic Plan Update
  Mr. Craig Kuennen, Deputy General Manager, provided an update on GWP’s Strategic
  Plan. Mr. Kuennen described GWP’s vision, mission, and core values: excellence,
  integrity, honesty, trust, fairness, teamwork, respect, accountability, compassion, cultural
  awareness. Mr. Kuennen presented GWP’s progress on critical initiatives in six areas of
  strategic focus: Affordability and Fiscal Responsibility; Exceptional Customer Service;
  Workforce; Sustainability; Automation, and Innovation.

  Mr. Kuennen responded to questions from the Commissioners. In response to a question
  from Commissioner Avanessian, Mr. Kuennen stated that GWP’s area of most
  tremendous success over the past year is in the areas of affordability and Fiscal
  Responsibility and Exceptional Customer Service; and GWP’s area of greatest challenge
  was about reliability, due to COVID-19 making it challenging for crews in the field.
  Commissioner Flanigan wondered if it might be time to update GWP’s goals to make them
  more rigorous where warranted, potentially in the area of electric vehicles and Time-of-
  Use rates. Mr. Kuennen concurred that the goals are a few years old and should be
  revisited and updated. Commissioner Lall suggested that GWP’s goals should be
  updated to reflect GWP's core values as a municipal utility, including sustainability and
  innovation.

  2
 4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Mr. Jerry Johnson (requesting temporary abatement of GWP Demand Charge rate for
  commercial customers during COVID-19).

5. AGENDA FORECAST
  The Commissioners reviewed the agenda forecast for the November and December 2020
  meetings.

  Commissioner Lall requested a discussion regarding the governor’s announcement on
  electrification of the vehicle fleet over the next 10-15 years and the impact of that on GWP.
  Commissioners Flanigan and Jazmadarian concurred.

  Commissioner Flanigan requested a discussion of options on demand charge relief for commercial
  customers. Commissioners Lall and Avanessian concurred.

6. ADJOURNMENT
  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Lall
  Seconded by: Commissioner Avanessian
  Motion Passed.
  The meeting was adjourned at 5:53 p.m.
